fullPassage:
Art & Our Environment

While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. Let us take a look at a few modern artworks that address environmental issues.

The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks rally people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to highlight the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.

He says, "You can't order a product online without having it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, made of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue because at the end of the day, you know, companies and governments can't ignore the interest of the consumers. At the same time, we also need to pressure governments and corporations to do the right thing."

The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. They are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more acidic. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will dissolve.

Kendler says, "I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage collective action and collective responsibility. One thing that art can do really well is to help us imagine how the world might be otherwise. Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it."

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to appreciate the world around them. "I believe we've separated ourselves from nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it," says Ching.

One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another. "I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. My call to action is to remember the magic and wonder of this planet."

Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, ring especially true in this context. "They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself."

Banksy's New Work in Port Talbot

Secretive street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth. When you look around the corner, however, you realize that the child's mouth is open to ash coming from a dumpster fire.

Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot resident, to create art that would highlight Port Talbot's dust problem. Owen believed that the area's children were facing serious health risks by playing in the dust coming from the local steel plant.

Children are particularly defenseless against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 93% of the world's children under 15 breathe in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even estimated that about 600,000 children died from exposure to polluted air.

Banksy's art has included environmental messages before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a child with a can of red paint and the words, "I remember when all this was trees."

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주변을 ①바라보는 방식. 문제를 ②다루는 데에. 환경 문제를 ③다루는 현대 예술. Benjamin Von Wong ④에 의한 사진.
det.analysis: ✅ ① looking: ways of + V-ing. 전치사 of 뒤 동명사. ❌ ② address → addressing: 'in addressing'에서 전치사 in 뒤 동명사 필요. ✅ ③ address: 관계대명사절의 동사. artworks(복수) + address. ✅ ④ by: 수동태 행위자 표시 전치사.
det.tip: 전치사 in + V-ing: 'in addressing(다루는 데에)'. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 옴.

questions.passage: You can't order a product online without ①<u>having</u> it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, ②<u>made</u> of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer ③<u>find</u> it harder and harder to opt out. I think it is important for you ④<u>to inform</u> your friends and family of the issue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 플라스틱 포장 없이 ①배달시키는 것. 플라스틱으로 ②만들어진. 개인 소비자는 빠져나오기가 ③어렵다고 느끼다. 친구에게 ④알리는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① having: without + V-ing. 사역동사 have + 목적어 + p.p. ✅ ② made: be made of. 수동태. ❌ ③ find → finds: 주어가 the individual consumer(3인칭 단수). finds가 맞음. ✅ ④ to inform: It is important for you to V. 가주어-진주어 구문.
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(the individual consumer) + 동사 finds. 주어-동사 수일치 확인.

questions.passage: She covered an old boom box with various shells, ①<u>which</u> took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as ②<u>calming</u> ocean sounds. They are actually ③<u>that</u> she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid. She wanted us ④<u>to think</u> of what sea creatures might go through one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그것들을 모으는 데 1년이 걸렸는데, ①그것들은. ②잔잔한 바닷소리. 사실 그녀가 ③녹음한 것이다. 우리가 ④생각하기를 원했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① which: 계속적 용법 관계대명사. 선행사 shells를 부연 설명. ✅ ② calming: 현재분사로 ocean sounds 수식. '잔잔하게 하는'. ❌ ③ that → what: 'what she recorded'에서 선행사 포함 관계대명사 what 필요. that은 선행사 없이 쓸 수 없음. ✅ ④ to think: want + O + to V. 올바른 구문.
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that/which. 선행사가 없을 때 what 사용. that은 선행사 필수.

questions.passage: Most of his work, ①<u>including</u> this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to appreciate the world around them. One cannot help but ②<u>smile</u> at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is ③<u>how</u> he blends the features of one life form with ④<u>that</u> of another.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 그림을 ①포함하여. 미소를 짓지 않을 수 ②없다. ③어떻게 섞는지. 다른 생명체의 ④그것.
det.analysis: ✅ ① including: 전치사적 분사. 'including this painting'. ✅ ② smile: cannot help but + 동사원형. ✅ ③ how: 간접의문문 how he blends. ❌ ④ that → those: 앞의 the features(복수)를 대신하므로 those(복수 대명사) 사용. that은 단수.
det.tip: that(단수) / those(복수): 앞에 나온 명사의 수에 일치. the features → those.

questions.passage: His artworks ①<u>rally</u> people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to ②<u>highlight</u> the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to ③<u>opt out</u>. At the same time, we also need to ④<u>relieve</u> governments and corporations to do the right thing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들을 ④집결시킨다. 사실을 ②강조하다. ③빠져나오다. 정부와 기업을 ①안심시키다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① rally: 원문 그대로. 집결시키다. ✅ ② highlight: 원문 그대로. 강조하다. ✅ ③ opt out: 원문 그대로. 빠져나오다. ❌ ④ relieve → pressure: 정부에 '압력을 가하다'가 원문. relieve(완화하다)는 반대 의미.
det.tip: pressure(압력을 가하다) ↔ relieve(완화하다, 안심시키다). 맥락: 정부에 옳은 일을 하도록 요구.

questions.passage: I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 담화를 ①촉발하다. 큰 ②변화를 만들다. 진실처럼 ③들리다. ④우리 자신이 바꿔야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① strike up: 원문 그대로. 대화를 시작하다/촉발하다. ✅ ② difference: 원문 그대로. make a great difference. ✅ ③ ring: 원문 그대로. ring true(진실처럼 들리다). ❌ ④ ourselves → yourself: 원문은 'change them yourself'. 주어 you에 맞는 재귀대명사는 yourself.
det.tip: 재귀대명사는 주어에 일치: you → yourself. ourselves는 we에 대응. 원문: you actually have to change them yourself.

questions.passage: The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks rally people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to highlight the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

det.korean: 첫 번째 예술 작품은 Benjamin Von Wong의 사진(photograph)이다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 본문에 'a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong'이라고 명시. 사진이지 조각이 아님.
det.tip: photograph(사진) ≠ sculpture(조각). 지문의 핵심 정보를 정확히 읽어야 함.

questions.passage: The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. They are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
Jenny Kendler의 작품에서 들리는 소리는 실제 바다 소리를 녹음한 것이다.

det.korean: 그 소리는 실제로 그녀가 유치를 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 것이다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 'something you may regard as calming ocean sounds'이지만 실제로는 'she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid' — 유치가 산에 녹는 소리를 녹음한 것. 실제 바다 소리가 아님.
det.tip: 함정: '바닷소리라고 여길 수도 있는' 것이지 실제 바다 소리가 아님. 유치가 산에 녹는 소리.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
WHO에 따르면 전 세계 15세 미만 어린이의 약 93%가 매일 유독성 공기를 들이마신다.

det.korean: 전 세계 15세 미만 어린이의 약 93%가 매일 유독성 공기를 들이마신다.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 본문에 'about 93% of the world's children under 15 breathe in toxic air every day'라고 정확히 일치.
det.tip: 숫자 정보(93%, 15세 미만, 매일)가 모두 원문과 일치하는지 확인.

According to the passage, art has the power to not only convey beauty but also __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: reduce the public's interest in social issues
change how we perceive the world around us

det.korean: 예술은 아름다움을 전할 뿐 아니라 우리가 주변 세계를 인식하는 방식을 바꿀 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'change our ways of looking at our surroundings' = 주변을 바라보는 방식을 바꾸다. ❌ ①: 전통적 소통 방식 대체 — 언급 없음. ❌ ②: 사회 문제에 대한 관심 감소 — 반대. ❌ ④: 환경 문제 완전 제거 — 과장.
det.tip: perceive = '인식하다'. change how we perceive = change our ways of looking at.

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Kendler의 예술은 사람들이 바다를 보호하기 위해 개인적, 공동의 행동 모두를 취하도록 격려한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 본문에 'encourage collective action and collective responsibility' 직접 언급. ❌ ①: private steps — 개인적 조치는 언급되지만 '비공개 조치'는 아님. ❌ ③: 예술적 조치 — 맥락 무관. ❌ ④: 경제적 결정 — 언급 없음.
det.tip: individual(개인적) ↔ collective(공동의). both A and B 구조에서 대조되는 단어 찾기.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Jon Ching은 자연에 대한 무관심을 주제로 한다.
Jon Ching은 인간이 자연을 단순히 소비하고 있다고 말한다.
Jon Ching은 인간이 자연을 잘 보호하고 있다고 말한다.

det.korean: 자연이 번성하도록 돕는 것이 아니라 단순히 소비하고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 'we are simply consuming it' 원문 직접 인용. ❌ ①: painting(그림)이지 photograph(사진)가 아님. ❌ ②: celebration of nature(자연 예찬)이지 무관심이 아님. ❌ ③: '보호하고 있다'가 아니라 '소비하고 있다'.
det.tip: painting(그림) ≠ photograph(사진). 선지 ①의 함정 주의.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Banksy의 작품은 바다 오염 문제를 강조한다.
Banksy의 작품에서 아이가 잡으려는 것은 사실 쓰레기통 불에서 나오는 재이다.

det.korean: 아이의 입은 쓰레기통의 불길에서 나오는 재를 향해 열려 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'the child's mouth is open to ash coming from a dumpster fire' 원문 그대로. ❌ ①: Port Talbot의 콘크리트 차고에 나타남. ❌ ③: Gary Owen은 Banksy에게 요청한 주민. ❌ ④: dust problem(먼지 문제)이지 바다 오염이 아님.
det.tip: snowflakes(눈송이) vs ash(재): 처음에는 눈송이를 잡는 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 재.

questions.passage: ①The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong that rallies people around environmental actions. ②His work titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap highlights the fact that plastic enters the ocean in large quantities every hour. ③Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, making it hard for consumers to opt out. ④Von Wong believes that informing friends and family about this issue is important because companies and governments cannot ignore consumers' interests.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문의 내용과 다른 부분이 포함된 문장은?

det.korean: ②에서 'every hour(매시간)'는 원문의 'every minute(매분)'와 다르다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 원문 그대로. ❌ ②: 'every hour' → 원문은 'every minute'. 시간 단위가 다름. ✅ ③: 원문 내용과 일치. ✅ ④: 원문 내용과 일치.
det.tip: every minute(매분) ≠ every hour(매시간). 숫자/단위 변경 함정에 주의.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Jenny Kendler의 작품에서 나오는 소리의 실제 정체를 서술하시오.
questions.wa: 유치를 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 소리
accept: 유치를 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 소리
아기 이빨을 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 소리

det.korean: 사실 이 소리는 그녀가 자신의 유치 하나를 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 것이다.

det.tip: baby teeth = 유치(젖니). dissolve = 녹다/녹이다. acid = 산(酸).

questions.ans: 유치를 산에 녹일 때 녹음한 소리

Banksy's New Work in Port Talbot

Secretive street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Jon Ching이 자신의 작품에서 '단순히 잘못된 것을 깊이 생각하기보다' 표현하고자 하는 것을 본문에서 찾아 **영어**로 쓰시오.

det.korean: 잘못된 것을 깊이 생각하기보다 밝은 희망(a silver lining)을 표출하는 것이 필요하다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong'. silver lining = 어두운 상황 속 밝은 면.
det.tip: silver lining = '구름 뒤 은빛 테두리' → '어두운 상황 속 밝은 희망'. 관용표현.

questions.passage: Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, ring especially true in this context. "__________, but you actually have to change them yourself."

[ say / always / time / they / changes / things ]

det.korean: 사람들은 시간이 상황을 바꾼다고들 항상 말한다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'They always say time changes things'. 주어(They) + 빈도부사(always) + 동사(say) + 목적절(time changes things).
det.tip: 빈도부사(always)는 일반동사(say) 앞에 위치. 목적절 내부: time(주어) + changes(동사) + things(목적어).

questions.ans: They always say time changes things

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. Let us take a look at a few modern artworks that address environmental issues.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the history of modern art movements
the economic value of environmental art
the role of art in addressing environmental issues
the technical skills needed to create artworks

det.korean: 환경 문제를 다루는 예술의 역할.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 본문은 예술이 환경 문제를 다루는 데 필수적 역할을 한다고 서술. ❌ ①: 현대 미술 운동의 역사 — 주제 아님. ❌ ②: 경제적 가치 — 언급 없음. ❌ ④: 기술적 기량 — 언급 없음.
det.tip: 주제문: 'art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues'.

questions.passage: Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot resident, to create art that would highlight Port Talbot's dust problem. Owen believed that the area's children were facing serious health risks by playing in the dust coming from the local steel plant. Children are particularly defenseless against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸에 가장 적절한 것은?
Banksy's artwork in Port Talbot was created to draw attention to the (A)__________ problem that puts local (B)__________ at risk.

det.korean: Banksy의 작품은 지역 어린이들을 위험에 빠뜨리는 먼지 문제에 주목하기 위해 만들어졌다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: dust problem(먼지 문제) + children(어린이들). 원문 직접 언급. ❌ ②: noise(소음) — 먼지가 아님. ❌ ③: workers(근로자) — 어린이가 아님. ❌ ④: water(물) — 먼지가 아님.
det.tip: dust(먼지) from the local steel plant. children이 health risks에 직면.

det.analysis: not only A but also B 구문. strike up conversations = 담화를 촉발하다. make a great difference = 큰 변화를 만들다. by inspiring us to take action = 행동을 취하도록 고무함으로써.
det.tip: not only A but also B = A뿐만 아니라 B도. strike up = '시작하다(대화 등)'. make a difference = '변화를 만들다'.

questions.ans: Art can not only strike up conversations about the environment, but also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action.
